properties.decision: What the reader sees, for a claim no route holds. Built: it reads "contested" when at least one route would hold were the dispute under it settled, naming what stands against each such route; "unproven" when no route is held up by a dispute. The cogito's "I exist" has three readings: two are contested, the third (performance) lacks a premise for another reason, and it reads contested. Options: (a) one contested route is enough, as built; (b) every route must be contested, so "I exist" would stay "unproven". Recommended: (a): a reader is told the claim would stand if the dispute went its way, and "unproven" keeps its meaning of nothing holding it up. It is wrong if a reader should be told a route is missing for other reasons before being told the claim is disputed; the why names the other routes either way.
properties.name: IDEA (proposed 2026-10-20, phase 6 PR 2): does a claim read contested when ONE of its routes is held up only by a dispute (built), or only when EVERY route is?
properties.no_relation_note: Governs cap:a-claim-held-up-only-by-disputes-reads-contested (drawn next); its near matches are the requirement and the cogito trial fact it was built from.
properties.rationale:
The requirement's name says "every route", its statement "every line of support held up only by standing objections or contested premises", and its measured case (the cogito) has a third route unsupported for another reason, yet was observed and recorded as "all three routes were only contested". (a) fits the measured case; (b) fits the name.
